rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Like human life surpasses animal life, the believer endowed with knowledge, faith, certainty, and devotion has a higher life, perception, and will than ordinary human life.
rows.anchor: فلنقض في الإنسان الذي أوتي العلم والإيمان واستقر في دار الإيقان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise of a good life in 16:97 shows that believers possess a life that is good in its own nature and exceeds life in the unqualified sense.
rows.anchor: فلهم الحياة لكنها بطبعها طيبة وراء مطلق الحياة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Disbelievers have counterparts of believers' hearts, eyes, and ears, but lack their perfected effects, evidence of a real difference in spiritual life.
rows.anchor: يثبت لهم أمثال القلوب والأعين والأذان التي في المؤمنين لكنه ينفي كمال آثارها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that God supports believers with a spirit from Him further shows their distinctive spiritual life is real.
rows.anchor: حتى أثبت لهم روحا خاصا بهم فقال أولئك كتب في قلوبهم الإيمان وأيدهم بروح منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believer's life and light are actual realities, not merely figurative expressions; God's special believers have a stronger claim to the name life than ordinary people.
rows.anchor: أن للحياة وكذا للنور حقيقة في المؤمن واقعية وليس الكلام جاريا على ذاك التجوز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dead person is one inwardly astray or an unbeliever before faith; God revives him through faith or guidance, which have the same sense here.
rows.anchor: أي ضالا من حيث نفسه أو ضالا كافرا قبل أن يؤمن بربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The light given to the believer is knowledge that grows out of faith.
rows.anchor: وجعلنا له نورا أي علما متولدا من إيمانه

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: A report transmitted by both Muslim groups says that whoever acts on what he knows is granted knowledge of what he did not know, or God teaches him what he did not know.
rows.anchor: من عمل بما علم رزقه الله علم ما لم يعلم أو علمه الله ما لم يعلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When faith's spirit settles in a person, it reshapes opinions and deeds to fit it; any settled virtue or vice similarly reshapes thoughts and actions.
rows.anchor: فإن روح الإيمان إذا تمكنت من نفس الإنسان واستقرت فيها حولت الآراء والأعمال إلى صور تناسبها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The proposal that the light means faith or the Qur'an is unlikely in this context.
rows.anchor: وربما قيل إن المراد بالنور هو الإيمان أو القرآن وهو بعيد من السياق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believer uses this light to discern a dark social path, choosing deeds that benefit his happiness and avoiding those that harm it.
rows.anchor: يتبصر به في مسير حياته الاجتماعية المظلمة ليأخذ من الأعمال ما ينفعه في سعادة حياته

words: كَمَن مَّثَلُهُۥ فِى ٱلظُّلُمَٰتِ لَيْسَ بِخَارِجٍۢ مِّنْهَا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unbeliever remains in darkness because death does not produce the effects of life; there is no prospect that he will find afterlife-benefiting deeds or salvation.
rows.anchor: لأن الموت لا يستتبع آثار الحياة البتة فلا مطمع في أن يهتدي الكافر إلى أعمال تنفعه في أخراه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase is elliptical: its estimate is ‘he is in the darknesses, not leaving them,’ with an omitted subject pronoun returning to the relative pronoun.
rows.anchor: ففي الكلام مبتدأ محذوف هو الضمير العائد إلى الموصول

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another grammatical estimate is ‘like one whose likeness is that of someone in darkness’; al-Tabataba'i accepts it if not for the excessive ellipsis.
rows.anchor: وقيل التقدير كمن مثله مثل من هو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The simile in ‘thus’ takes the preceding parable as a model and states a general rule, as in the Qur'anic parables of truth and falsehood and of examples.
rows.anchor: من قبيل تشبيه الفرع بالأصل بعناية إعطاء القاعدة الكلية

words: كَذَٰلِكَ زُيِّنَ لِلْكَٰفِرِينَ مَا كَانُوا۟ يَعْمَلُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unbelievers' deeds have been adorned to attract and imprison them in darkness, preventing escape into happiness and light; God does not guide wrongdoers.
rows.anchor: تجذبهم إليها وتحبسهم ولا تدعهم يخرجوا منها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A reported reading compares these unbelievers, whose disbelief was adorned, with the earlier believers whose faith was adorned; al-Tabataba'i finds it far from context.
rows.anchor: وقيل إن وجه التشبيه في قوله

words: وكذلك جعلنا في كل قرية أكابر مجرميها
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The next verse parallels those given light with people left in darkness: town leaders are made into plotters against religion, the Prophet, and believers, but their plots do not help them.
rows.anchor: جعلنا في كل قرية أكابر مجرميها ليمكروا فيها بالدعوة الدينية والنبي والمؤمنين لكنه لا ينفعهم

words: وكذلك جعلنا في كل قرية أكابر مجرميها
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On this reading, adornment explains why their deeds cannot free them from darkness, while the following verse explains that their plotting harms themselves rather than others.
rows.anchor: مسوق لبيان أن أعمالهم ومكرهم لا يضر غيرهم

words: وكذلك جعلنا في كل قرية أكابر مجرميها
rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says God made the disbelievers' deeds attractive and town criminals plot just as He made believers bear light; believers chose guidance, while criminals chose error and were enabled to plot.
rows.anchor: وقيل معنى التشبيه في الآية أن مثل ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guidance is of two kinds: creational direction of each kind and individual toward its created perfection, acts, appointed course, and lifespan; the Qur'an describes God as giving each thing its form and then guiding it.
rows.anchor: وهدايته تعالى نوعان أحدهما الهداية التكوينية وهي التي تتعلق بالأمور التكوينية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Legislative guidance concerns true beliefs and righteous acts prescribed through commands and prohibitions, with reward promised for obedience and punishment threatened for neglect.
rows.anchor: والنوع الثاني الهداية التشريعية وهي التي تتعلق بالأمور التشريعية من الاعتقادات الحقة والأعمال الصالحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Legislative guidance can show the road, as in 76:3, or bring someone to the destination, as in 7:176.
rows.anchor: ومن هذه الهداية ما هي إراءة الطريق كما في قوله تعالى إنا هديناه السبيل

words: فمن يرد الله أن يهديه يشرح صدره للإسلام
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God defines guidance as a special openness of heart that recognizes truth and righteous action without constraint and is ready to submit to His commands and judgments.
rows.anchor: فهي انبساط خاص في القلب يعي به القول الحق والعمل الصالح من غير أن يتضيق به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expanded heart is described as being on light because it distinguishes what it should accept—true speech and sound action—from false speech and corrupt action.
rows.anchor: وقد وصفه في الآية بالنور لأنه ينجلي به للقلب ما يجب عليه أن يعيه من التسليم لحق القول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A defining mark of divine guidance is that it brings its recipients onto a straight, sound path without deviation or contradiction.
rows.anchor: من خاصة الهداية الإلهية أنها تورد المهتدين بها صراطا مستقيما وطريقا سويا لا تخلف فيه ولا اختلاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The path's teachings fit one unchanging divine unity and human nature; every prophet calls to the same religion, with differences only between general and detailed expression.
rows.anchor: فالذي يدعو إليه نبي من أنبياء الله هو الذي يدعو إليه جميعهم

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
rows.claim: In al-Kafi, Zayd says Imam al-Baqir glossed the dead person as one who knows nothing, the light as an imam followed, and the person in darkness as one who does not know the Imam.
rows.anchor: عن زيد قال سمعت أبا جعفر عليه السلام يقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabataba'i treats the Imam gloss as an application to a particular case; the context requires life to mean faith and light to mean divine guidance to true belief and righteous action.
rows.anchor: أقول وهو من قبيل الجري والانطباق فسياق الآية يأبى إلا أن تكون الحياة هو الإيمان والنور هو الهداية الإلهية

rows.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
rows.claim: Al-Durr al-Manthur cites Zayd ibn Aslam as saying the verse was revealed about Ammar ibn Yasir; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: عن زيد بن أسلم أن الآية نزلت في عمار بن ياسر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وزيد بن أسلم
rows.claim: Al-Durr al-Manthur reports from Ibn Abbas and Zayd ibn Aslam that the verse concerned Umar ibn al-Khattab and Abu Jahl; al-Tabataba'i says the context rules out restricting it to them.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس وزيد بن أسلم أنها نزلت في عمر بن الخطاب وأبي جهل بن هشام والسياق يأبى كون الآية خاصة

words: فمن يرد الله أن يهديه يشرح صدره للإسلام
rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: Al-Durr al-Manthur lists Ibn Abi Shayba, Ibn Abi al-Dunya, Ibn Jarir, Abu al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh, al-Hakim, and al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab reporting through Ibn Mas'ud from the Prophet: God's light opens the heart; its signs are longing for the hereafter, detachment from worldly deception, and readiness for death.
rows.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

words: فمن يرد الله أن يهديه يشرح صدره للإسلام
rows.speaker: أبو جعفر المدائني والفضل والحسن وعبد الله بن السور
rows.claim: Al-Tabataba'i says several exegetes also transmit the heart-light report from the Prophet through the Successors Abu Ja'far al-Mada'ini, al-Fadl, al-Hasan, and Abd Allah ibn al-Sawr.
rows.anchor: عن جمع من التابعين كأبي جعفر المدائني والفضل والحسن وعبد الله بن السور عن النبي

words: فمن يرد الله أن يهديه يشرح صدره للإسلام
rows.speaker: علي بن موسى الرضا عليه السلام
rows.claim: Asked by Hamdan ibn Sulayman, al-Rida says guidance by worldly faith and toward paradise opens the chest to submission, trust, and assurance; disbelief and disobedience leave it constricted, doubtful, and unstable.
rows.anchor: عن حمدان بن سليمان النيشابوري قال سألت أبا الحسن الرضا عليه السلام عن قول الله

words: فمن يرد الله أن يهديه يشرح صدره للإسلام
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabataba'i says the Imam's report contains fine points that indicate the explanation he has given above.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث نكات حسنة تشير إلى ما شرحناه في البيان المتقدم

words: فمن يرد الله أن يهديه يشرح صدره للإسلام
rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Tabataba'i adds that al-Ayyashi transmits the previous report mursal and al-Saduq transmits it with a chain in al-Tawhid from Imam al-Sadiq.
rows.anchor: ورواه العياشي في التفسير مرسلا والصدوق في التوحيد مسندا عنه عليه السلام

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: In al-Kafi, al-Halabi reports from Imam al-Sadiq that the heart struggles in the chest seeking truth and becomes settled when truth reaches it; the Imam recites the verse.
rows.anchor: عن الحلبي عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال إن القلب يتلجلج في الجوف يطلب الحق فإذا جاء به اطمأن وقر

rows.speaker: موسى عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Ayyashi gives a similar account from Abu Jamila, from Abd Allah ibn Ja'far, from his brother Musa, that the heart seeks truth and settles when it finds it.
rows.anchor: ورواه العياشي في تفسيره عن أبي جميلة عن عبد الله بن جعفر عن أخيه موسى عليه السلام

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
rows.claim: Abu Basir reports from Khaythama that Imam al-Baqir described the heart's movement up to the throat until it finds truth, then settles; he folded his fingers and recited the verse.
rows.anchor: عن أبي بصير عن خيثمة قال سمعت أبا جعفر عليه السلام يقول إن القلب يتقلب من لدن موضعه إلى حنجرته

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: Imam al-Sadiq explains haraj to Musa ibn Ashim by closing his fingers: it is like a solid object into which nothing enters and from which nothing leaves.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبد الله عليه السلام لموسى بن أشيم أتدري ما الحرج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabataba'i notes that al-Burhan attributes a similar report to al-Saduq, al-Barqi transmits its opening through Khaythama from al-Baqir, and the gloss of haraj fits the earlier lexical explanation from al-Raghib.
rows.anchor: وروى ما يقرب منه في تفسير البرهان عن الصدوق وروى صدر الحديث البرقي في المحاسن عن خيثمة

words: فمن يرد الله أن يهديه يشرح صدره للإسلام
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The delegation given to the Prophet and the Imams means they were taught inexhaustible readings of God's Book and authorized to disclose whichever they wished; the analogy is Solomon's delegated discretion in 38:39.
rows.anchor: مسألة التفويض إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم والأئمة من ولده وإن وردت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabataba'i allows that reciting the verse may allude to that delegation, but says its apparent purpose here is to describe hearts, prompted by Musa ibn Ashim's distress.
rows.anchor: وإن كان الظاهر أن المراد به بيان حال القلوب بمناسبة ما ابتلى به موسى بن أشيم

rows.speaker: القمي
rows.claim: Tafsir al-Qummi compares the constricted heart to a tree crowded by surrounding trees so that its branches cannot spread sideways and continue upward in the sky; the image fits al-Raghib's gloss of haraj.
rows.anchor: تفسير القمي في الآية قال قال مثل شجرة

words: كذلك يجعل الله الرجس على الذين لا يؤمنون
rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Ayyashi reports from Abu Basir that Imam al-Sadiq glossed the impurity placed on unbelievers as doubt.
rows.anchor: وفي تفسير العياشي عن أبي بصير عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام

words: كذلك يجعل الله الرجس على الذين لا يؤمنون
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabataba'i treats the gloss of impurity as doubt as an application that identifies one instance of the verse.
rows.anchor: أقول وهو من قبيل التطبيق وبيان بعض المصاديق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These verses continue the preceding discussion by explaining how God makes some wrongdoers guardians over others, such as Satans over unbelievers, without injustice: on Judgment Day they will admit their shirk and sins followed their own choice after warning.
rows.anchor: بيان الآيات متصلة بما قبلها وهي تفسر معنى ولاية بعض الظالمين بعضا المجعولة من الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Divine decree does not remove the choice on which accountability rests, and human choice does not conflict with decree: God decrees their chosen following of Satan rather than compelling it.
rows.anchor: فالقضاء الإلهي لا يسلب عنهم الاختيار الذي عليه مدار المؤاخذة والمجازاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God has no need of anything they possess that could justify oppression; He created them in mercy and urged them to mercy, but they wronged themselves and failed.
rows.anchor: بل الله سبحانه غني عنهم لا حاجة له إلى شيء مما بأيديهم حتى يظلمهم لأجله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istakthara min means to do much of a thing or action; the jinn's taking much from humanity refers to their seduction and authority, not to physically bringing humans together, whom God creates and gathers.
rows.anchor: يقال أكثر من الشيء أو الفعل واستكثر منه إذا أتى بالكثير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The jinn's ‘many’ are people over whom they exert influence through guardianship and seduction, not human bodies they gathered.
rows.anchor: وإنما للشياطين الاستكثار مما هم مسلطون عليه وهو إغواء الإنس من طريق ولايتهم عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their mutual guardianship is a voluntary exchange: followers seek benefits from the leader, while leaders seek advantage in managing their followers; neither side is compelled.
rows.anchor: وليست بولاية إجبار واضطرار بل من قبيل التعامل من الطرفين يتبع التابع المتبوع ابتغاء لما يرى في اتباعه من الفائدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jinn enjoy tempting and ruling humans; humans enjoy following whispers and suggestions to obtain material pleasures and satisfy their desires.
rows.anchor: فللجن نوع التذاذ من إغواء الإنس والولاية عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human followers enjoyed worldly ornament and desires through Satanic suggestions, while the jinn enjoyed the humans' obedience to their whispers.
rows.anchor: فتمتعنا بوساوسهم وتسويلاتهم من متاع الدنيا وزخارفها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The appointed term means the limit and degree attained through their deeds—the final level of their actualized existence—not the time their lifespans end; by choosing mutual enjoyment they reached a sinful, unbelieving state.
rows.anchor: الحد الذي قدر لوجودهم والدرجة التي حصلت لهم من أعمالهم دون الوقت الذي ينتهي إليه أعمارهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The context may indicate that ‘jinn’ here refers specifically to the devils among the jinn who whisper into people's breasts.
rows.anchor: وإنما للشياطين الاستكثار مما هم مسلطون عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mathwa is a place of settled residence, from thawa, to remain; ‘the Fire is your abode’ therefore means a settled place from which they will not leave, reinforced by ‘abiding forever.’
rows.anchor: والمثوى اسم مكان من قولهم ثوى يثوي ثواء أي أقام مع استقرار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception preserves God's power to take them out of the Fire even though He will not do so.
rows.anchor: استثناء يفيد أن القدرة الإلهية باقية مع ذلك على ما كانت فله مع ذلك أن يخرجكم منها وإن كان لا يفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ending that God is Wise and Knowing explains the judgment stated in the verse; the address is to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وهو يفيد تعليل البيان الواقع في الآية والخطاب للنبي

words: وكذلك نولي بعض الظالمين بعضا بما كانوا يكسبون
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verse 129 explains God's making of some wrongdoers guardians over others: followers gain from a leader's seduction, incur sins, and are placed under that leader's guardianship.
rows.anchor: فيه بيان أن جعله تعالى بعض الظالمين أولياء يجري على الحقيقة المبينة في الآية السابقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition bi can express cause or recompense; the guardianship is retribution for prior wrongdoing, not an initial appointment without earlier sin, as in 2:26.
rows.anchor: أن هذه التولية إنما هي بنحو المجازاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse shifts from third-person reference to first-person speech to disclose this truth particularly to the Prophet; first-person address suits confidential speech.
rows.anchor: وقد التفت في الآية من الغيبة إلى التكلم ليختص النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم ببيان هذه الحقيقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The next address answers an objection: although people chose their path, they might plead ignorance that their sins and pleasures would bring ruin and lasting misery, making punishment of the heedless seem unjust.
rows.anchor: في هذا الخطاب دفع دخل يمكن أن يتوجه إلى الحجة السابقة المأخوذة من اعترافهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hamula are the larger livestock able to carry loads; farsh are the smaller animals, as if spread on the ground or trodden like a carpet.
rows.anchor: الحمولة أكابر الأنعام لإطاقتها الحمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to eat permits eating and affirms what reason already indicates, like the preceding permission to eat fruit in 6:141.
rows.anchor: إباحة للأكل وإمضاء لما يدل عليه العقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Not following Satan's steps here means not moving to prohibit what God made lawful; al-Tabataba'i has explained Satan's steps as forbidding the lawful without knowledge.
rows.anchor: أي لا تسيروا في هذا الأمر المشروع إباحته باتباع الشيطان بوضع قدمكم موضع قدمه بأن تحرموا ما أحله

words: ثمانية أزواج من الضأن اثنين ومن المعز اثنين
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The detailed listing of eight pairs expands the general livestock account to intensify blame across every form; ‘eight pairs’ appositionally clarifies ‘pack animals and those spread on the ground.’
rows.anchor: تفصيل للأنعام بعد الإجمال والمراد به تشديد اللوم والتوبيخ عليهم ببسطه على كل صورة

words: ومن الإبل اثنين ومن البقر اثنين
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A zawj may mean one member paired with another or the two together; sheep, goats, cattle, and camels make four kinds, or eight male-female pairs, and the questions challenge which sexes or womb contents God forbade.
rows.anchor: ويطلق الزوج على الواحد الذي يكون معه آخر

words: ومن الإبل اثنين ومن البقر اثنين
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The camel and cattle pairs and the following challenge about males, females, and womb contents are clear in light of the preceding explanation.
rows.anchor: ومن الإبل اثنين ومن البقر اثنين

words: ومن الإبل اثنين ومن البقر اثنين
rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A reported view takes the two pairs at each of the four mentions to mean domestic and wild animals.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد بالاثنين في المواضع الأربعة من الآيتين الأهلي والوحشي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse presents one side of an implied alternative: did they know this through reason or transmitted information, or were they witnesses who heard God prohibit it directly?
rows.anchor: هذا شق من ترديد حذف شقه الآخر على ما يدل عليه الكلام

words: فمن أظلم ممن افترى على الله كذبا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question follows because they have no answer; ‘one who fabricates’ replaces ‘you’ to identify the cause of their injustice—lying against God to mislead without knowledge—and explain why wrongdoers are unguided.
rows.anchor: تفريع على ما قبله باعتبار دلالته على انقطاعهم عن الجواب وعلى ذلك فمعناه فمن أظلم منكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabataba'i says the meaning of the statement about what is forbidden to eat is apparent.
rows.anchor: قل لا أجد فيما أوحي إلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every clawed animal means one having a nail-like bone growing at the tips of its fingers.
rows.anchor: الظفر واحد الأظفار وهو العظم النابت على رؤوس الأصابع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-hawaya means the entrails, or bowels.
rows.anchor: والحوايا المباعر

words: إِلَّا مَا حَمَلَتْ ظُهُورُهُمَآ أَوِ ٱلْحَوَايَآ أَوْ مَا ٱخْتَلَطَ بِعَظْمٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Majma' offers nominative coordination of al-hawaya with ‘backs’ or accusative coordination with the object of ‘carried’; al-Tabataba'i prefers the nominative. The phrase ‘what mixed with bone’ coordinates with the first ‘what.’
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون نصبا عطفا على ما في قوله
